text:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — Acme POC wants private deploy. They expect bursts up to ~6Gbps sustained for 30s and occasional 20Gbps spikes for <10s. Asking whether PrivateLink interface endpoint can handle that and what MTU/tuning we recommend. Also need firewall rules they can hand to infra. :thinking:

Jess Rivera: PrivateLink (AWS interface endpoint) is limited by ENI bandwidth and the customer’s subnet/NAT throughput. For 6Gbps sustained I'd recommend Dedicated or ensure the ENI instance type supports that. VPC peering to our customer VPC with TGW might be better for raw bandwidth.

Nora Patel: For firewall rules — customer only needs outbound to our privatelink endpoint IPs on TCP 443 (mTLS). If they're using proxy/inspect, ensure SNI passthrough or TLS origination offload. Sample SG:
```
Type: HTTPS
Protocol: TCP
Port: 443
Source: <customer-cidr>
Description: Allow egress to Redwood Private endpoint
```
Also ensure MTU 1500 across tunnel; if they have jumbo frames, recommend 9001 end-to-end and confirm NAT/edge devices preserve it.

Sam O'Neill: Pricing/POC note — host egress in Private deployments is billed on committed BW if Dedicated, otherwise metered. If they expect sustained 6Gbps during the POC we should quote reserved throughput or temporary burst credits. I'll open an ops pricing note.

Alex Chen: @Jess does PrivateLink preserve client source IP? Customer needs source IP for audit logs.

Jess Rivera: Interface endpoints don't preserve original client IP — traffic originates from the ENI. If preserve-client-ip is required, use VPC Peering or Transit Gateway where traffic flows directly. Alternatively, put a proxy in the customer VPC that forwards the original IP in an X-Forwarded-For header.

Nora Patel: Firewall snippet (for on-prem/proxy egress):
```
# Allow to Redwood Private endpoints
allow tcp from CUSTOMER_NET to 10.0.12.0/28 port 443
# If using NAT egress
allow tcp from NAT_IP to 52.12.34.56 port 443
```

Sam O'Neill: Also check the TLS cipher policy — require TLS1.2+ and mTLS certs. We need their CA bundle for onboarding.

Alex Chen: Can we get a short list of IP ranges they should allow? They prefer a small set for firewall. :pray:

Jess Rivera: We'll give per-region endpoint IPs (typically a /28). I'll extract the endpoint ENI IPs once the PR is created. For the POC we can propose using our static egress IPs if they want fixed allowlist; that adds a small surcharge.

Sam O'Neill: FYI — raised ticket #INC-5483 for bandwidth quota and asked finance to draft a POC overage estimate.

Nora Patel: Quick tests to ask customer to run: iperf3 from their edge to our endpoint subnet + curl with --resolve to test TLS/mTLS handshake. That'll validate MTU and TLS.

Alex Chen: Great. I'll collate and send to customer. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
